situation:
You are a twenty-year-old community college student with a checking account at WESTBROOK COMMUNITY CREDIT UNION. A member services representative (judge) has agreed to meet with you and hear how you plan to cover a shortfall in that account this week.

Your hours were cut, a rent payment posted anyway, and your debit card overdrew the account by two hundred fourteen dollars. The credit union charges an overdraft fee for every day the balance stays negative. Your first credit card carries a six-hundred-dollar balance against a one-thousand-dollar limit, and a parent co-signed that card, so the same balance sits on the parent's credit record.

Taking a cash advance on the credit card would clear the negative balance today, but it would push the balance near the limit and lower your credit score and the parent's along with it.

You also hold a target date retirement fund in a Roth IRA you opened on a phone app that asked for no minimum deposit. Selling part of that fund would leave both credit records untouched, but it would spend money set aside for retirement and give up years of compounding growth. The app reports the fund has returned about seven percent a year, well under the card's cash advance rate.

The representative (judge) wants you to compare what each course costs, recommend one, and say how you would explain it to the parent whose credit record carries the card. The representative (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after you have presented and answered the questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of a member services representative (judge) at WESTBROOK COMMUNITY CREDIT UNION.

Background is the same as the situation above. The student's account is overdrawn by two hundred fourteen dollars, the credit union charges an overdraft fee for every day the balance stays negative, the first credit card carries a six-hundred-dollar balance against a one-thousand-dollar limit with a parent as co-signer, and a target date retirement fund sits in a Roth IRA opened on a phone app.

You have asked the student (participant) to compare what a cash advance and a sale of the fund would each cost, to recommend one, and to say how the decision would be explained to the parent who co-signed the card.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: What are you going to tell the parent who co-signed the card?
If the credit score drops, how do you explain that to them?
